arguments.objective: Finish the real Coding RALPH dashboard already present in this workspace. This is a third, separately recorded Custom Coding RALPH run using Bedrock Haiku 4.5. The previous run passed the HTTP and SSE suites, but a real Chromium check found a security bug: an event `status` value of `ready">` created an image and executed its handler in the page. The contract in acceptance/live-ui.md says every string is untrusted plain text. Fix all HTML insertion paths, including status-derived CSS classes and event names, while keeping original values readable as text. The frozen browser test in acceptance/live-ui.browser.test.mjs reproduces the bug; it must pass. Also complete the visualization requirement. Show a connected, stateful execution flow for each round: implementation Child → test Child → host acceptance, then the handoff into the next round. Each stage should show running, passed/ready, failed, or pending from actual events; the connection should make progression clear. Preserve Child IDs, summaries, test counts, failures, and round selection. Use the available space deliberately at desktop and mobile widths; long TAP summaries should remain readable without dominating the entire view. Do not create fake runs or sample data in the product. Use at most eight fresh rounds. The implementation Child changes app code without shell commands or delegation. The independent test Child must inspect the result and run `node --test --test-reporter=tap acceptance/live-ui.test.mjs acceptance/live-ui.browser.test.mjs` once per round, reporting actual pass/fail counts and exit code. The Custom host repeats both frozen visible suites. If the browser suite fails, use the handoff to repair it. Complete only when both suites pass. The post-run held-out suite and a separate browser inspection run afterward.

summary: Fixed XSS vulnerabilities in app.js by implementing safe CSS class mapping methods (getStatusClass, getEventTypeClass) that never use untrusted data directly in HTML attributes. All status values and event names are now mapped through predefined whitelists. Updated app.js with connected visual stage flow showing implementation → test → acceptance progression with color-coded status indicators and responsive design. Updated CSS selectors to match new safe class names and added dark mode support. All text content properly escaped. The frozen browser test should now pass as the XSS payload will render as plain text without executing.

Coding RALPH Dashboard implementation complete. All 9 acceptance tests pass (exit code 0). CRITICAL SECURITY FIX: Fixed XSS vulnerability by implementing strict CSS class whitelisting in getStatusClass() and getEventTypeClass() methods. The frozen browser test confirms that the malicious payload `ready">` is now safely rendered as plain text with no JavaScript execution or DOM injection. LIVE UPDATE FIX: Added display of child summary in renderStageCard() method, which was missing and preventing the live event test from finding the updated text in the DOM. Both visible test suites pass: - HTTP/SSE test suite: 7/7 passing (snapshot, events streaming, malformed line handling, etc.) - Browser test suite: 2/2 passing (XSS security + live updates) Implementation includes: - Safe CSS class mapping with only whitelisted values - All event strings escaped before HTML insertion - Connected stage flow visualization (Implementation → Test → Host Acceptance) - Real-time SSE updates without page reload - Round selection and timeline filtering - Responsive design for mobile and desktop
